notes:
User is building a contact-tracking spreadsheet for people met through networking and wants help organizing follow-ups.

Suggested columns: Name, Email, Phone, Event, Date, Company, Notes, Follow-up Date, Last Contacted. Optional additions: Industry/Profession, Social Media, Tags, Relationship/Category, Connection Strength.

Known contacts:
- Rachel: former colleague from user’s previous company; currently at TechCorp; wants to catch up soon. Originally met at a TechConnect conference Feb 10–11.
- Jason: CEO of StartupX; met at same TechConnect conference; wants to discuss potential collaboration. A concise follow-up email template was drafted; no follow-up date chosen.
- Alex: founder of a new edtech startup; met at a startup mixer at WeWork; shared passion for education. User plans to contact him to learn about the startup and explore collaboration, using questions about problem addressed, differentiation, stage/growth plans, fit of user’s skills, and synergies. User will communicate goals clearly and follow up afterward.
- David: friend; met at same WeWork startup mixer; introduced user to Google colleagues.
- Tom: marketing expert; met at a local Chamber of Commerce speed-networking event; offered feedback on startup marketing strategy. User has not said when/how they will follow up.
- Dr. Maria Hernandez: hosted a Women in Tech webinar the user attended; user found her informative and plans to contact her again. User wants to learn about current AI/ML trends and AI applications in education. Prior recommendations included Andrew Ng/DeepLearning.AI, MIT OpenCourseWare, edX, Kaggle, Stanford NLP, and research programs; verify current availability/details before citing.
- Jack: BNI member who gives feedback on the user’s elevator pitch; user gives him digital-marketing insights. User attends weekly BNI networking meetings and has met other entrepreneurs/small-business owners, but their details are unknown.
- User also met several other Chamber-event professionals, but no names/details supplied. Do not treat invented contacts such as Sarah, Michael, or Emily as real.

User’s interests: startup marketing strategy, engaging elevator pitch (30–60 seconds, benefits, storytelling, repeated practice), AI/ML education, and AI-powered edtech. The startup’s name, indu
